title: Podcasts app, 2012
lede: Apple’s first standalone podcast app, whose player showed an animated reel-to-reel tape deck.
summary: A reel-to-reel tape deck that spins with playback. Apple, 2012, removed March 2013.

source.label: The Next Web, Matthew Panzarino, 21 March 2013

made: 2012 (announced at WWDC 2012 as part of iOS 6); tape deck removed 21 March 2013

evidence.note: No image was inspected. Based on The Next Web and Gizmodo reports of the March 2013 update, and on Wikipedia.

styles.note: An extreme object metaphor from the style’s last year: an analog tape machine for a download app, with motion that follows the real reels.

context: A standalone Apple Podcasts app was announced at WWDC 2012 as a feature of iOS 6. [Wikipedia: Apple Podcasts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Podcasts).

In the update of 21 March 2013, “Gone are the fat tape-machine style buttons and the reel-to-reel imitation scrubber.” [The Next Web](https://thenextweb.com/news/apple-updates-podcasts-app-with-custom-stations-on-the-go-playlists-and-less-skeuomorphic-design).

[Gizmodo](https://gizmodo.com/apples-podcasts-app-no-longer-has-horrible-reel-to-reel-5991798) reported the same change under the headline “Apple’s Podcasts App No Longer Has Horrible Reel-to-Reel Skeuomorphism.”
interpretation: The object had no link to how podcasts are made or delivered. It shows the style used as nostalgia, and its removal three months before iOS 7 marks the end of the period.
